body:
Cycle-2 audit measurements (6 chats x 10 topics, English and Chinese; 20 targeted + 20 unrelated prompts):

| | today | proposed |
|---|---|---|
| precision | 40% | 95% |
| recall / top-1 | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| unrelated prompts with a block | 7 of 20 | 0 of 20 |
| injected tokens | 8,235 | 3,411 |

Chosen design: gate on raw evidence (label/alias word = 2, gist word = 0.5; floor 3, i.e. two label words or one plus two gist words), never on a rarity score (rarity-gated recall collapsed from 20/20 to 17/20 at 300 topics); rarity only orders ties. Then a coverage cut: a lower hit is kept only if it matches a prompt word that no higher hit already explained, which stops generic words ('cache', 'key') from dragging extra topics in. Shown ids are dropped after the cut, with no back-fill. CJK: bigrams made only of particles/pronouns or only of hiragana are not search words.

Cycle-2 audit measurements: the turn-1 list costs 406 tokens at 12 chats and 632 at 50 (84 of them a header repeating the recall syntax), and first-prompt titles often say nothing ('hi' was a React login chat). A ranked one-line-summary list measured 207 tokens at 12 chats and 187 at 50.

Chosen design: the builder writes `"summary"` (one line, about 12 words) in its existing JSON (about +35 input and +14 output tokens per build, no extra call). The list shows `c9 <summary>` for chats with topics only, ranked by overlap with the first prompt then recency, within a 200-token budget, with a short header using placeholders (`recall("c<chat>")`). Until a chat is rebuilt, its line falls back to dsh's own title (#41) plus its top topic labels.

Cycle-2 audit measurements: with the transcript first, two consecutive builds share 3-5 prefix tokens (0%). With [fixed rules][existing topics in insertion order][transcript], the shared prefix is 874 / 2,444 / 5,682 tokens at 50 / 200 / 500 topics (29 / 53 / 73% cacheable). The full topic list stays (it is what lets the model reuse ids); anything per-chat or per-time goes after it so the cached part never changes.

Cycle-2 audit measurements (150 chats, 9,185 topics): the pre-step took 186 ms, of which 92 ms was re-tokenizing every label, alias and gist on each message and 37 ms reading files. A per-topic token memo plus a stat-keyed read cache took it to 14 ms. Also part of this cycle: #49 (redundant matches and loads).

Cycle-2 audit: dsh's base bundle mounts `sessionQuery` at the profile root; `observeSession(sid, { signal, projectionMode: 'none' })` returns a disposable observation with the events (readEvent is capped at 50 events). It is read with `ctx.get` per call, never injected (cordis has no optional inject). Privacy gate: another chat's turn is served only when it lies within that chat's indexed span (`seq <= builtSeq`) and at or after its own fork point, so turns after `/context-graph off`, never-indexed turns, and a private parent's turns inherited by a shared fork are never exposed. Legacy folders without a dsh log fall back to stored messages.
